question: Would the engine's index earnings-yield anchor and its bond carry anchor, computed only with information available at each date, have forecast the next 12-month total return better than the expanding historical mean?

data.source: data/history/valuation/shiller-monthly.csv.gz (Shiller: monthly average S&P composite price, 12-month dividends and earnings, CPI, 10-year Treasury rate GS10)
data.inspection_before_registration: file layout and first/last dates only; no returns or anchors computed

equity_anchor.engine_formula: prior + confidence * (earnings_yield + inflation - prior), dist/assets/js/return-model.mjs valuationAnchor
equity_anchor.earnings_yield: E(t-3 months) / P(t): earnings assumed public with a 3-month lag
equity_anchor.inflation: CPI(t-1)/CPI(t-13) - 1: trailing 12 months, one-month publication lag; replaces the 10-year breakeven, unavailable before 2003
equity_anchor.realized: prod over k=0..11 of (P(t+k+1) + D(t+k)/12) / P(t+k) - 1

bond_anchor.engine_formula: carry = yield to maturity at the cut (base regime, no fee)
bond_anchor.realized: buy a 10-year par bond with coupon GS10(t) at t; after 12 months value the remaining 9-year bond at GS10(t+12) with annual coupons; return = price + coupon - 1

benchmark: expanding mean of all realized 12-month returns that matured by the origin, from 1871
test: one-sided Clark-West adjusted MSE difference on the 119 nonoverlapping origins, t statistic with ordinary standard error
not_tested: international equity ETFs: no free history of their P/E
constituent-based anchors of US equity ETFs and stocks: no point-in-time fundamentals
limits: The earnings-yield idea comes from a literature that studied this same Shiller series, so the test is not independent of that literature. Monthly average prices, not month-end closes. No result changes the engine or the fund.
